Source size: as first produced, the workspace was about 470 MB as a gzipped tar, mostly kernel-checked certificate data. For this submission the files outside the import closure were dropped, and the 2612 certificate bodies in the GlobalRepellingData*.lean files are written as `fast_case% "..."`, a compact decimal form that a syntax macro (Submission/Codec/FastCase.lean) expands back to exactly the same terms. The compact form stores each disk centre as a branch choice (0 or 1) plus a small correction to the exact preimage of the matching disk of the previous step, and leaves out the five check bounds of each cell, which the macro recomputes as the tightest values the checker accepts (the values every certificate already stored). Every certificate is still checked by `decide +kernel`, and no axioms are added. The submitted tree is 26.8 MB as a gzipped tar; the commit message lists the changes.

Produced by Humanfia's LOT (Lean Option Tree) orchestrator: agent sessions recursively split the statement into frozen sub-obligations, prove them in parallel, and every step is checked with the official lean-eval checker (comparator, nanoda and Lean kernel replay). The proof is fully machine-written; humans built the orchestrator and the seed package, chose the external code the run could use, and operated the infrastructure. It follows the route of Pardon's proof (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 26 (2013)).

Builds on Mathlib and lean-pool, which is imported as a dependency (projects imported: Brouwer, ClassificationOfSurfaces, FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup, HopfProblem, JacobianDiffgeo, PLAcceleratedNesterovLean, Polytopes, RiemannMappingTheorem, SardMoreira, Schoenflies). Some files of the proof contain code copied or adapted from lean-pool projects (Brouwer, ClassificationOfSurfaces, EhrhartVolumeInequality, FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup, HopfProblem, JacobianDiffgeo, SardMoreira, Schoenflies), and four files are modified copies of, or new code around, three files on cell triangulations from OpenAI's `openai/math` repository (Apache-2.0). Each such file keeps its copyright and attribution header. `NOTICE` at the tree's root lists the imported libraries, every piece of copied or adapted code with its licence, and where each of those files now is; the licence texts are in `LICENSES/` (lean-pool's LICENSE, Brouwer's MIT licence, and the NOTICE and LICENSE that come with the cell-triangulation code).

The submitted tree holds only the import closure of the theorem's module: 5271 Lean files under `Submission/`. To fit the evaluation's 4-core time limit, they are joined into 1083 modules: 4672 files form 484 merged modules, and 599 files are kept as they are. Files are joined only along their imports, and only when every file that imports one of them already imports all of them, so no module sees more names than before. Each joined file's text appears unchanged between the lines `-- ====== begin <original path> ======` and `-- ====== end <original path> ======`: first its header comments, then its text after the imports, inside its own `section ... end` (with an `end` added for each section or namespace the file leaves open). The statement and every proof are unchanged. Size: 1099 files, 9.67 MB as a gzipped tar.

Checked before submission with the official comparator setup (comparator d03acab, lean4export 076e8e5, nanoda 68d5ca9, Lean kernel replay; permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice) in an isolated container: "Your solution is okay!" for this tree (with the problem's `PROBLEM.md`, which the checker expects; the submitted tree leaves it out as in our other submissions). This check took 43 min at 16 CPUs (container memory peak 21.3 GiB). Measured on a runner-sized container (4 CPUs, 15 GB memory, Lean-Eval's layout with lean-pool built from source), the whole check took 2 h 47 min (2 h 25 min of it compiling), with a comparator peak of 8.0 GiB and at most 3.5 GiB for any single Lean process.

Models: GPT-6.1 sol (through Codex) and Claude Opus 5.5.

This is the proof of #2181 ported to the supported `stable` setup (Lean v4.36.0, Mathlib fc4f59e5); #2181 was rejected only because its toolchain (v4.35.0-rc3) is no longer supported. The port was made mechanically by Claude Opus 5.5, outside the orchestrator: 9 edits in 7 files (3 case names `h` -> `ind` for Mathlib's `Nat.strong_induction_on`, 3 explicit arguments where v4.36.0 elaborates differently, 3 `set_option linter.concreteInstances false in` where Mathlib's new linter times out); no proof was restructured. `NOTICE` records the edits.

Note on the Model field: "Humanifa + GPT 5.6 sol" is the public label our team (Humanfia) has used for its earlier lean-eval submissions, kept here for consistency. It is a team identity, not the list of models used.

Produced by Humanfia's LOT (Lean Option Tree) orchestrator: agent sessions recursively split the statement into frozen sub-obligations, prove them in parallel, and every step is checked. The proof is machine-written; humans built the orchestrator and the seed package and operated the infrastructure. The run took 1.9 h of wall-clock time.

The run started from a seed package of ours that contains code by others, with attribution (see `NOTICE` and `LICENSES/` in the submitted workspace):
- LeanCondensed by Dagur Asgeirsson et al. (https://github.com/dagurtomas/LeanCondensed, commit 339ecc99, Apache-2.0), the repository this problem is extracted from: 34 files under `Submission/Seed/LeanCondensed/`, ported to the benchmark's Lean and Mathlib, rebased onto the challenge's `ChallengeDeps`, with every declaration that used `sorry` removed. The first three holes (`solidification`, its additivity and `solidificationAdjunction`) are LeanCondensed's solidification functor and adjunction.
- Part of the singular homology (barycentric subdivision, small chains, excision, Mayer-Vietoris) of a Lean library of differential geometry built by members of our team, Apache-2.0; authors (its CITATION.cff): Yuan Liao, Ziyang Qin, Jui-Hui Chung, Ayush Khaitan, Zhengyang Zhang, Hongzhou Lin, Zijian Zhang, Ligeng Zhu, Peng Lu, Bennett Chow. 15 files under `Submission/Seed/dglib/`.
Everything else under `Submission/` (about 11.9k lines) was written by the run: the derived solidification functor as the left adjoint of the derived inclusion and its identification with the total left derived functor, and the comparison of the derived solidification of ℤ[X] with singular chains for Hausdorff CW complexes.

Hole 8 (`derivedSolidificationFreeCWFunctor`) is universe polymorphic as in the challenge; holes 9-12 force universe 0, where it is the real composite. For a universe `u > 0` it is a constant functor: universe-0 light condensed abelian groups have no ℤ[X] for such X, and no other hole constrains it (comment in `Submission/Obl/Root.lean`).

Checked before submission (this port, exact submitted bytes): Lean-Eval's own evaluator, the toolchain's `lake test` with `lake comparator` (bubblewrap 0.12.0; NanoDa and the Lean kernel; permitted axioms propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice), in a 16-CPU / 32 GB sandbox with the setup's pinned packages read-only: "Your solution is okay!", 1564 s, memory peak 13.4 GB; an independent rerun gave the same verdict.

Problem `gorenstein_walter`, on Lean-Eval's previous-stable configuration (Lean v4.35.0).

This proof is not our work, and no model produced any of its content. It is the public theorem `CFSG.GorensteinWalter.gorenstein_walter` of AxiomMath/CFSG (https://github.com/AxiomMath/CFSG, commit 965a0775, Apache-2.0). AxiomMath's Gorenstein-Walter proof originally comes from Qiuzhen-CFSG (https://github.com/Qiuzhen-CFSG/CFSG, Apache-2.0), which is vendored in that repository, and it builds on Mathlib and TauCeti. The theorem is imported through the `cfsg` dependency that the previous-stable configuration provides for solution imports (lean-eval #720); no CFSG file is copied or changed. All credit belongs to their authors.

Our only content is in `Submission.lean`: one `import CFSG.Dihedral.GorensteinWalter` and one `exact CFSG.GorensteinWalter.gorenstein_walter G hnonab P _hdih`, plus an attribution comment. The theorem's statement is the Lean-Eval statement (alpha-equivalent, same universe parameters; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). All other files are Lean-Eval's own previous-stable render of the problem (lean-eval bcc14246). `NOTICE` and `LICENSES/AxiomMath-CFSG/LICENSE` (Apache-2.0) carry the attribution.

There was no proof search. Our infrastructure agent (Claude Opus 5.5) prepared the workspace and wrote the one-line bridge as an operations task. The Model field says this: the proof comes from AxiomMath CFSG, not from a model.

Checked before submission on the exact submitted bytes with Lean-Eval's own evaluator (`lake test` -> `lake comparator`; NanoDa and the Lean kernel; bubblewrap, no network, 16 CPUs / 32 GB): "Your solution is okay!" in 1,098 s, memory peak 10.4 GB.
